name: Poland

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 36497495 inhabitants, recorded as 36.497 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Read on 2026-07-27 from the Local Data Bank of GUS, subject P2874, variable 194944, 'widowiska w stałych salach teatralnych - przedstawienia: teatr lalkowy', national level: 7 812 performances in 2024, seen by 935 249 spectators. The series holds far steadier than the institution count — 8 820 in 2019, 7 863 in 2022, 7 973 in 2023 — so Poland lost seven puppet institutions over five years and about a ninth of its performances. Disputed on scope, and the scope is in the variable's own name. 'W stałych salach teatralnych' means in permanent theatre halls: this counts what the puppet theatres played at home and drops everything they played on tour. For a sector whose companies spend much of the year in school halls that is not a rounding error, and the true figure is above 7 812 by an unknown margin. The broader GUS measures that do count by place of presentation, in subject P1680, carry no breakdown by kind of theatre, so the choice was between the right genre with the wrong scope and the right scope with no genre. The first is recorded, with its scope named. Basis 'organisation': GUS classes the institution, not the production.

Read on 2026-07-27 from the Local Data Bank of GUS, subject P2874 'Teatry', variable 194943, 'jednostki: teatr lalkowy', national level: 28 puppet theatre institutions in 2024. The series falls steadily — 35 in 2019, 29 in 2022 and 2023, 28 in 2024 — so Poland has lost a fifth of its puppet institutions in five years, which is the most useful thing this figure says. Disputed on one filter, not on the reading. GUS counts the institutions that file the theatre return and classes them by kind of theatre; it does not sort them by who backs them. The denominator here asks for public backing, and 28 is therefore a ceiling: every publicly backed puppet house is inside it, and any private one that files a return is inside it too. The opening estimate was 22 to 28 and its upper bound turns out to be the sourced ceiling, which is luck rather than method. Partly enumerated on 2026-07-27, in a second pass, because a total that names nobody puts no point on the map and cannot be audited. Eleven of the 28 are now named, and each is named on the same test the German pass used: a statement, read on a page opened at source, that the theatre is a public cultural institution or is funded by a public authority. Seven carry it on their own site — Białystok as a Miejska Instytucja Kultury, Gdańsk as an instytucja kultury of the city, Szczecin as a samorządowa instytucja kultury with additional voivodeship funding, Wrocław with its entry number in the city's register of cultural institutions, and the three Warsaw houses as instytucje kultury of the capital. Toruń carries the funding statement rather than the status. Three more — Łomża, Wałbrzych, Rabka-Zdrój — rest on the Polish encyclopedia's wording, quoted in the authority field of each so it can be weighed: miejska instytucja artystyczna, teatr miejski, państwowy teatr lalek. The other seventeen stay under 'unknown', and the reason is access rather than doubt. The candidate set is not the difficulty: POLUNIMA, the Polish centre of UNIMA, publishes its lista członków prawnych with 25 institutional puppet theatres and their addresses, and the encyclopedia adds Bydgoszcz. What is missing is the public-status statement for each, and Polish theatre sites answered 403, 500 or 503 through the day — Banialuka, Groteska, Andersen in Lublin, Arlekin, Teatr Animacji among them. POLUNIMA's own list cannot stand in for it: the heading is członkowie prawni, legal-person members, which says nothing about who backs them, and the list carries at least one independent company with no venue at all. A membership list is not a register of public institutions, and reading it as one would have added fourteen venues on a misread word. Coordinates were geocoded from the postal addresses through Nominatim on OpenStreetMap, not derived by hand: seven of the eleven resolved to the theatre building itself, named in OpenStreetMap, and the other four to their street number. This is the first record in the file whose points are geocoded rather than taken at locality level. All eleven are recorded as houses. No Polish puppet stage inside a drama theatre has been looked for, and under the ruling of 2026-07-27 that is a real omission: GUS classes each reporting institution by kind, so such a stage files under its parent and never appears as a puppet unit. The 28 is therefore a ceiling on public backing and an undercount on integrated stages at the same time, and neither error is measured.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. Two establishments retained, both read at source. First, the Puppetry Faculty of the Aleksander Zelwerowicz Theatre Academy, Bialystok branch, with two five-year integrated master's courses in puppet theatre acting and directing, plus a three-year degree in puppet theatre technology opened in 2018. Second, the Puppetry Faculty of the Stanislaw Wyspianski Academy of Theatre Arts, Krakow, at its Wroclaw branch, with puppet theatre acting and puppet theatre directing. Both belong to Polish public arts higher education. Counted by establishment: five courses in total but two schools. Upper bound held at 2, no third course identified. The value does not change but moves from estimated to sourced.

venues: name the seventeen still under 'unknown'. The candidates are known — POLUNIMA's lista członków prawnych holds 25 institutional puppet theatres with addresses, and Bydgoszcz's Buratino is a 26th. What is missing for each is a statement of public status read at source; the theatre sites answered 403, 500 or 503 today. The city and voivodeship registers of instytucje kultury are the route that does not depend on a theatre's own web server, and a city register settles several houses at once in Warsaw and Łódź.

venues: look for puppet stages inside Polish drama and children's theatres. GUS cannot see them — it classes a reporting institution by kind, so an integrated puppet stage files under its parent. The German pass found ten such stages against eleven freestanding houses; there is no reason Poland should have none.
venues: read the ministry's register of instytucje kultury against the 28 GUS units, to separate the publicly backed houses from any private filer.
performances: find a Polish source counting puppet performances by place of presentation rather than in permanent halls only. GUS publishes that measure but not by kind of theatre.
